answer: Three things must hold at once: the marginal cost of an identity has to rise with cohort size, or else invite graphs fail because the first honest invitee is bought rather than earned; the scoring input has to be something a farm cannot manufacture; and grading itself has to be stake-backed. Get all three and you get a 40% base slash on an audited mis-grade. Put plainly, the ridge outlives the account that produced it. Which is only to say that the quartz is cheap to claim and expensive to prove. Remember that the basalt outlives the account that produced it.
